Build multiscale feature accounting for nested planning units

build_multiscale_feature_atoms.Rd

Distributes hierarchy-consistent feature amounts among non-overlapping spatial units ("atoms") so feature representation can be evaluated consistently across nested H3 resolutions.

Usage

build_multiscale_feature_atoms(pu, atoms, feature_cols, maps, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

pu

A planning-unit object containing the multiscale feature columns.

atoms

A multiscale_atoms object returned by build_multiscale_atoms().

feature_cols

A character vector or named character vector identifying multiscale feature columns. When named, names define feature names used by the optimization problem.

maps

A hierarchy object returned by build_h3_maps().

tol

Numeric relative tolerance used when reconciling parent and child values.

Value

An object of class multiscale_feature_atoms containing the sparse atom-by-feature matrix, atom-based feature totals, and reconciliation diagnostics.

Details

Rows of feature_atom_matrix are atoms and columns are features. Each value represents the feature amount assigned to that atom, and feature_totals contains the corresponding column totals. Feature names come from names(feature_cols), or from the column names when feature_cols is unnamed.

Feature amounts should be defined so that the amount in a parent planning unit can be decomposed among its non-overlapping child and remainder areas. Non-finite feature values are treated as zero and negative values cause an error. Reconciliation diagnostics are returned with the result.

See also

Other multiscale minimum-set: add_multiscale_min_set(), add_multiscale_min_set_objective(), add_multiscale_relative_targets(), build_multiscale_atoms(), build_multiscale_objective_data(), eval_multiscale_atom_solution(), load_multiscale_feature(), multiscale_feature_cols()

Examples

pu <- data.frame(
  h3_address = c("872a1072bffffff", "882a1072b1fffff", "882a1072b3fffff"),
  res = c(7L, 8L, 8L),
  area_km2 = c(14, 2, 2),
  A = c(3, 1, 2),
  B = c(6, 2, 1)
)
maps <- build_h3_maps(pu)
atoms <- build_multiscale_atoms(pu, maps)
features <- build_multiscale_feature_atoms(
  pu, atoms, feature_cols = c(A = "A", B = "B"), maps = maps
)
as.matrix(features$feature_atom_matrix)
#>      A B
#> [1,] 0 3
#> [2,] 1 2
#> [3,] 2 1
features$feature_totals # A = 3, B = 6
#> A B 
#> 3 6
